column1: title
Compiling a kernel on first use got faster by refusing to include PyTorch's giant header and moving the bookkeeping to Python
Cutting one long sequence's keys into chunks so 132 streaming multiprocessors are not left idle while one of them does all the work
Picking the next token stopped needing a sort, and stopped taking an unpredictable number of tries
Prompt work and one-token work stopped being two separate GPU launches, and started sharing one kernel that never ends
The attention kernel stopped paying a merge tax on work it never split, and the merge itself shrank from a whole thread block to a single warp
A filter that was asked to keep everything stopped searching for where to cut
One thread block now squeezes four tokens through the same barrier, and the launch stopped creating twice the blocks it needed
Finding the k best tokens stopped being a guessing game over values and became four passes over bytes, with the vocabulary parked in fast memory
The normalized activations stopped taking a round trip through memory in 16 bits before being squeezed into 4
A matrix multiply for eight rows stopped pretending it had a hundred and twenty-eight, by computing the transpose instead
Neighbouring thread blocks started reading each other's scratchpads, so picking the top k stopped going through main memory
A glue kernel that refused 8-bit inputs was blocking the whole 8-bit long-context path, and teaching it narrower loads unblocked it
The GPUs started shrinking their numbers to 8 bits before shipping them to each other, and spent their idle cycles doing it
Kernels that were rebuilt from scratch in every new process started being saved to disk and relinked in milliseconds
A fused expert-parallel mixture-of-experts kernel became usable inside a real serving engine, improving prefill throughput
The all-reduce tail of a tensor-parallel MoE layer got a hardware-native fused backend that picks its protocol by token count
On the selected GPU, the best attention kernel selector always picked the old one
A whole mixture-of-experts layer collapsed into one GPU kernel launch, for the eight-token batches that decoding actually produces
Picking the fastest matrix-multiply kernel was inefficient
The API server stopped paying an asyncio tax on every token: the engine moved to its own plain loop
Turning text into numbers stopped being done one request at a time: the API server now micro-batches tokenization
The server stopped sending one network message per generated token: buffer N tokens per reply
Several long prompts can now be read at once, and short prompts stopped getting stuck behind them
The scheduler stopped waiting for the GPU: it now plans step N+1 while step N is still running
The scheduler stopped reserving batch space for draft tokens that were never going to exist
Models learned to reuse a shared prompt: state-space snapshots are now cached at block boundaries
The attention cache learned to store keys and values in three or four bits, so a GPU holds several times more conversation
The KV cache for all layers of a block is now allocated in one contiguous chunk, so moving a block to or from the GPU is one large copy instead of dozens of small ones
Stopped writing the recurrent state back to GPU memory on every decode step, keeping a small ring buffer of recent inputs and replaying it instead
Stitched partial attention results together with a hand written kernel instead of a generic one
Rewrites the kernel that sorts tokens by expert so its counters fit in a few kilobytes of fast memory, and the three special case implementations collapse into one
Hands the whole mixture of experts block to vendor's own hand written kernels instead of running generic ones
The FP8 activation-quantization kernel got faster by reading 16 values per thread instead of 4
Turns skinny FP8 matrix multiplications sideways so the tensor core's fixed 64 or 128 row shape stops being mostly padding
The kernel that squeezes activations down to 4 bit numbers learns to fetch 32 bytes per thread instead of 16, and to spread its work across the long dimension
The bit-for-bit reproducible mode stops unpacking 8 bit weights into 16 bit ones before every matrix multiply, and instead runs a real 8 bit kernel pinned to one fixed shape
Rewrites the step that decides which speculated tokens survive as four kernels over a flat ragged layout, removing every CPU-GPU stall and every padded vocabulary-sized tensor
A speculative drafter can now guess seven tokens in one forward pass instead of seven
The all-reduce between GPUs and the normalization after it became one kernel
One request's KV cache is now split across GPUs by token position, so long contexts stop filling up memory
The whole decode step, attention included, can now be replayed as one CUDA graph, cutting per-token latency for small models
Attention setup code stopped asking the GPU questions it had to wait for
One number in a config file went from 512 to 1024, and a speculative-decoding workload got much faster
Switched top-k/top-p sampler to a custom set of kernels

Stopped re-reading a reasoning model's entire thought so far on every decode step just to check whether it has finished thinking, and instead looks up a single end token in the handful of tokens that are new
Rebuilt decode attention kernel around a matrix instruction that processes a 16 by 16 tile instead of a 4 by 4 one
Reads the KV cache faster during decode by switching to vendor's hand-written paged attention kernel
